issue_body:
### Description

`association_rules` coerces every NumPy scalar item identifier to `int`. This rejects NumPy string and byte-string labels, truncates floating-point labels, and can merge two distinct items into one before generating rules.

This occurs through the public frequent-itemset miners as well as with manually supplied itemsets:

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns import apriori, association_rules

transactions = pd.DataFrame(
    [[True, True], [True, False], [True, False], [False, True]],
    columns=pd.Index([np.float64(1.25), np.float64(1.75)], dtype=object),
)
itemsets = apriori(transactions, min_support=0.25, use_colnames=True)
rules = association_rules(itemsets, min_threshold=0)
print(len(rules))  # 0 on current master
```

Expected: two rules, `{1.25} -> {1.75}` and the reverse, each with support 0.25. The two confidences are 1/3 and 1/2. Instead, both identifiers become 1 and no rule is generated. Using `np.str_("milk")` and `np.str_("bread")` as the column labels raises `ValueError` instead.

### Proposed change and reproduction

Restrict the existing Python-integer normalization to NumPy integer identifiers. Preserve all other item values. Both ordinary metric calculation and `support_only=True` should preserve label identity.

Verified on unchanged master `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382` with 26 regression/control cases: 16 fail and 10 pass. The regressions include real `apriori` and `fpgrowth` paths. NumPy integer/boolean and ordinary Python labels are controls.

[Reproduction and fixed-source validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43664851871).
pr_body:
### Description

`association_rules` currently converts every NumPy scalar item identifier to `int`. NumPy strings and byte strings raise `ValueError`; floating-point identifiers are truncated, and distinct labels such as 1.25 and 1.75 collapse into one item, silently removing both otherwise-valid rules.

Restrict that normalization to NumPy integer identifiers. Other item values retain their identity in the generated antecedents and consequents. The change covers manually supplied itemsets and the real `apriori` / `fpgrowth` output paths. The integer normalization and metric formulas remain unchanged.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`. Validated source: `6dd107f2e41eba68e19454773b685d66632ba6fe`.

- The same 26 new regression/control cases produce **16 failures and 10 passes on unchanged production source**.
- With the fix, **all 137 frequent-pattern tests pass**, including the new cases and existing association-rule, Apriori, FP-Growth, FP-Max and H-Mine tests.
- Cases cover string, byte-string, float32, colliding float64, integer, boolean and tuple item labels, both support-only and ordinary metric calculation, complete rule/metric equivalence, explicit expected supports/confidences/lifts, and unchanged input data.
- Changed-file Black, isort and Flake8 checks pass. Validation restores the exact candidate source after the baseline run and verifies a clean working tree.
- Ubuntu, Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, pandas 2.3.3, SciPy 1.16.3 and scikit-learn 1.8.0, using the repository's frozen uv development environment. The existing frequent-pattern warning set remains; the full repository suite was not run.

[Completed validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43664851871).

### Related issues or pull requests

Checked all previous Afloat16 PRs and related all-state association-rule/item-identifier work. No equivalent change was found. The contribution contains only production code, regression tests, API documentation and a changelog entry; the validation workflow is maintained on a separate fork branch.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog note.
- [x] Added native regression/control tests.
- [x] Clarified item-identifier preservation in the public API docstring.
- [x] Ran the affected package tests and changed-file style checks.
